result.reasoning:
The float32 mechanism is real but immaterial, and the suggested fix is actively harmful.

(1) MECHANISM CONFIRMED, NOT DISPUTED. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/refute_es_boundary/mech.py: at M=241, float32 torch.nanquantile returns a value strictly below sorted[228] in 1703/3000 trials (float64: 0/3000, always exact). Root cause is narrower than reported: torch interpolates at frac = float32(0.95)*240 = 227.99999713897705, landing 2.86e-6 of the (s[227],s[228]) gap below s[228]. It is only representable in float32 when that gap exceeds ~2.1% of |s[228]|.

(2) THE CONVENTION IS BIT-IDENTICAL TO THE BASELINE THE RESEARCH COMPARES AGAINST, AND THE SUGGESTED FIX BREAKS IT. AlphaCube's day_quantile (src/alphacube/operators/dt_day.py:156) is literally torch.nanquantile(x, q, dim=-1, keepdim=True) - the same call _es_ratio makes. baseline_same.py: _es_ratio's selected set equals is_gt(x, day_quantile(x,0.95)) in 2000/2000 trials. The hand-written erm_* / h_es_ratio baselines select their tail exactly that way (see runs/F106_erm_mag_gap_1m/sweep_s3.json, studies/F106_erm_mag_gap_1m/hypo.yaml h_es_ratio). The documented purpose of day_es_ratio_hi (its own docstring, docs/new_operators.md, ~14 hypo3 'why' fields) is "the same quantity as erm_*, with the +1e-6 denominator replaced by a NaN guard" - which is apples-to-apples precisely because both sides share the same nanquantile + strict '>' in float32. Casting only _es_ratio to float64 makes it DISAGREE with the unchanged day_quantile baseline on 1178/2000 days (59%), injecting a second uncontrolled difference into the one comparison the operator exists to make. The cited cross_ema precedent is not one: its float64 cast fixes an overflow (amount-scale values squared, 1e16, ops_ext.py:178-181), not a comparison threshold.

(3) THE NaN SEMANTICS - THE OPERATOR'S ENTIRE POINT - ARE UNTOUCHED. nanflip.py: at lock durations 10/12/13/14/20/40/241 of 241 minutes, float32 and float64 agree exactly, including both NaN cases. The k=0 -> NaN guard never flips, because a tied top block spanning index 227 makes the interpolation exact, and the knife-edge exactly-13 case still rounds back to s[228] at price scale. Consequences: cross_valid_count(day_es_ratio_hi(Ret), 60) (F102, ut +4.7%/0.76) reads only NaN-ness and is bit-for-bit unchanged; F112's h3_es_hi_B, which explicitly relies on the k=0 branch to mask 一字板 days, still works.

(4) MOST REPORTED ROWS ARE UNREACHABLE (exact arithmetic, not simulation). reach.py: price-scale leaves 0/2000 affected (median gap/|v| = 6e-5 vs the ~0.021 threshold), so F112's day_es_ratio_hi(High) and F108's price-derived rows are immune. Widths other than 241 are immune outright: in_slice(Ret,2,237) and in_pct(Close,5) give n=236, 0.95*235 = 223.25, not an integer - so F101's three rows (ut ann -18.1%, -12.2%, -25.0%, the three largest magnitudes in the whole es_ratio set) and F109's in_pct row never touch the boundary. Only full-241 Ret (61%) and Amt (76%) leaves are exposed.

(5) MAGNITUDE IS BOUNDED AND SMALL. The change is exactly one extra minute in a 12->13-minute tail, so the relative change is (r-1)/(13r), bounded by 1/13 = 7.7%; measured mean 1.3% (Ret) / 3.0% (Amt), max 5.9% / 7.5%. The reported 2.9% is the max of their 500 normal draws, not a typical value.

(6) END-TO-END, INSIDE THE NOISE BAND. fair.py ran the real partura/books.py long-only pipeline (top 10% equal weight, excess vs the signalled+labelled equal weight, 15bp) on two panels built from IDENTICAL float32 minute bits (kernel vs float64), with the target driven by the latent AR(1) both panels estimate (neither privileged) at a realistic 2.5% daily sigma, at hl=20 (chosen by 41 of the 43 real rows) and reference long_sharpe in [-4.6,-0.8] - the real table's range: |dSharpe| mean 0.12 (Amt) / 0.21 (Ret), |dAnn| mean 0.62pp / 1.09pp, both inside the +-0.3 / +-3pp bands. Post-smoothing daily cross-sectional rank correlation 0.9997 (Amt) / 0.9979 (Ret); top-decile Jaccard 0.97 / 0.93. Each panel's |corr| with the latent truth differs by only 0.0007-0.0019, i.e. the float32 version is not measurably the worse estimator - the delta is sign-random reshuffling, not bias.

(7) NO REPORTED CONCLUSION RESTS ON AN es_ratio NUMBER. Across research/alpha_distillation/, day_es_ratio_hi appears exactly once: U2 in B01_reverse_guidance.md, a search-weight prior (w=2.0) over a pattern of eight operators, whose cited evidence is F107 h_gini_ema30 and F106 h_zero_minus_liq (gini / zero-ratio factors), not any es_ratio result. The 43 es_ratio rows are hypothesis-test rows that died decisively (-25.0%, -18.1%, -14.0%, -12.2%, -12.0%, -11.8%, -11.6%, -8.3%, -5.7% ann, |Sharpe| up to 3.9) or landed at +-2% ("dead" under the long-leg-net-excess criterion either way). The single positive, F103 cross_max(mul(day_close(Amt), day_es_ratio_hi(cross_decay_linear(Amt,30))), 5) at +13.7%/2.01, is Amt-flavored (+-0.6pp mean / +-1.6pp max) and unchanged. The six cov=0.00 rows are degenerate because the expression collapses, unrelated to this.

CAVEAT, stated honestly: the tail of the synthetic Ret-flavored distribution reaches |dSharpe| 0.63 and |dAnn| 3.50pp over 10 seeds, slightly outside the bands. That is a proportional (~2-3% of Sharpe) sign-random reshuffle, and it cannot move any row whose reported magnitude exceeds ~5pp - which covers every row from which a conclusion was actually drawn. Residual: I could not read the production store (no server access), so Ret's minute-0 finiteness is unverified; if Ret[...,0] is NaN then n=240, 0.95*239 = 227.05, and every day_es_ratio_hi(Ret) row is immune by width as well, strengthening the refutation.

result.corrected_fix:
Do NOT cast x to float64 inside _es_ratio alone - that is the one change that would actually damage the research, because it silently decouples day_es_ratio_hi/lo from the AlphaCube day_quantile + is_gt convention used by the hand-written erm_* / h_es_ratio baselines these operators were written to be compared against (disagreement on 1178/2000 days, 59%). The tolerance variant has the same problem for the same reason.

Preferred (zero cost, zero re-runs): leave /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:587-597 as it is and fix the docstrings of day_es_ratio_hi (line ~600) and day_es_ratio_lo (line ~611), which are the operator's definition per the module header ("The docstring of each kernel is its definition"). State that the threshold is the float32 torch.nanquantile value - the same primitive as day_quantile - and that at the production width M=241 the 95% point falls exactly on an order statistic, so a minute mathematically tied with the threshold may be included. This is precisely the convention day_topw_mean (ops_ext.py:576) already documents as "ties included" for the same boundary reason, so it makes the file self-consistent rather than introducing a second convention.

If a definitional change is genuinely wanted, do it jointly, not locally: add one shared helper (e.g. _q(x, q) that upcasts to float64 and returns both the threshold and the strict mask) and route BOTH alphacube day_quantile and _es_ratio through it, so the erm_* baseline and the new operator keep the same boundary convention; then re-run the affected rows, because that changes the baseline's numbers too. Note that AlphaCube is read-only for this work, so this is a request to the AlphaCube side, not a Partura-local edit.

In either case, restrict the claim to where it is reachable: full-241 Ret and Amt leaves only. Price-scale leaves (High, Close) and any leaf narrowed to 236 minutes by in_slice(x,2,237) or in_pct(Close,5) are immune, and the k=0 -> NaN guard is immune at every lock duration, so cross_valid_count(day_es_ratio_hi(Ret), 60) and F112's h3_es_hi_B need no revisiting.
